about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change. killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. A test that exists at base may still kill only through cases that change adds to it: before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run) before it was called a survivor. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent, and one that is not says why it is not killed. Every run was on macOS; the file has no code compiled for one platform only. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. Every run was on base_commit, with the file and its test module byte for byte as there (or as this change leaves the test module, for survivors_again).

runs.command: each mutant's edits applied as exact text, then cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge -E 'test(/hsn|invoice/)'

as the hand run with every bridge test (-E 'all()'), after the unmutated tree passed all 5079, for the twenty-two hand-written mutants the filtered run missed and the one the tool's run missed. Three of them (H68, H74, H81) first failed one test each, in tests that read no HSN/SAC path (a post run's master-mark check, and an outstandings read cut at a 300 ms deadline); both tests passed five runs of five alone on the unmutated tree, and the three were run again against every test and missed there, which is the verdict recorded
as the whole_set run, for the twenty-three still missed there (twenty-two hand-written, one from the tool)
